questions.statement: "Connection refused" usually means a firewall dropped the traffic.
questions.explanation: Refused means the machine answered but nothing listens on that port. A firewall that drops traffic makes the connection hang.

questions.statement: If DNS, TCP and TLS all work and the server returns 5xx, the network is fine and the application is broken.
Machines in a private subnet can reach the internet directly.
questions.explanation: Public subnets can reach the internet directly; private ones go through NAT or not at all.

questions.statement: dig reads /etc/hosts before asking the DNS server.
questions.explanation: dig asks the DNS server directly. Programs use the resolver library, which also reads /etc/hosts. getent hosts shows what programs really get.

questions.statement: A bastion (jump host) is the one machine reachable from outside, through which you reach the private ones.
A firewall rule with REJECT says nothing back, while DROP answers "refused".
questions.explanation: It is the other way around: DROP says nothing, REJECT answers refused.
